subject: science
title: Launch and diagnostic: systems and system models

standards.legacy_label: Science and engineering practice foundation - this unit claims no Michigan performance expectation.

essential_question: How do we reason honestly about systems too large, too slow, or too far away to experiment on?
learning_objectives: Observe the anchoring phenomenon, surface initial thinking about systems and system models without penalty, and pose a testable question.
Explain systems and system models using evidence, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
Apply systems and system models to a task the learner has not seen before, showing the reasoning that produced the result.
Check and revise the work on systems and system models against the stated success criteria and name the next step.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about systems and system models.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process, not a bare answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and identifies one specific next step.
Any quantity the learner reports is one the learner measured, computed, or cited to a named published source.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
pencil, keyboard, or other accessible response tool
printed or on-screen text, data table, or model for this lesson

lesson_flow.title: Retrieval and phenomenon check
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with the unit phenomenon - Two published graphs of the same climate record look like they tell opposite stories, purely because of their axes. - or a short retrieval prompt on systems and system models. Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, or question before any instruction. Record the prediction; it is not graded.

lesson_flow.title: Model or mini-lesson
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Develop systems and system models from the phenomenon: pose the testable question, build or use a model, and show how evidence constrains the explanation. Name the success criteria and demonstrate how to check the work. Phase focus: Launch and diagnostic.

lesson_flow.title: Guided practice
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Work two supported examples on systems and system models, asking after each move: what evidence or reasoning supports that step? Fade the prompting on the second example and have the learner narrate the check.

lesson_flow.title: Independent application
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: The learner completes a new application of systems and system models independently and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.

lesson_flow.title: Exit evidence and next step
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: In one concise response, the learner shows or explains the most important idea about systems and system models, then names one check that would catch an error or a weak claim in their own work.

student_activity: The learner completes a new application of systems and system models independently and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about systems and system models, then name one check that would catch an error or a weak claim.
scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target: accuracy, quality of evidence and reasoning, and evidence of checking or revision. Accept any valid approach that meets the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error. Do not award credit for a numerical result that the learner did not measure, compute, or cite to a named source.
extension_activity: Apply systems and system models under a new constraint, compare two approaches or two sources, or teach the idea with an original example. Extension never means completing another learner's graded work.

hazards.description: Desk-based work only; no chemicals, heat, electricity, or tools are used in this lesson.
hazards.mitigation: Materials are notebook, writing tool, and printed or on-screen text. Any hands-on extension defers to the unit investigation's safety review.

sensitivity: Content is academic; no personal, family, health, or location disclosure is requested.
stop_conditions: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.

Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.

A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.

Stores no raw reflection text, no free-text answers, no photograph, no video, and no voice recording.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Looking at the sun causes permanent eye damage.
MITIGATION: NEVER look at the sun directly, through any lens, grating, CD, camera, or filter. All solar work is done by measuring warming water in shade-versus-sun, with the learner's back to the sun.
HAZARD (physical): Working outdoors in sun risks heat and sunburn, and a sealed dark container left in full sun pressurises.
MITIGATION: Leave the water container OPEN - never capped or sealed - in the sun. Limit exposure to 30 minutes at a time, wear a hat and sunscreen, keep drinking water available, and work in the cooler part of the day.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. The published-data route is the DEFAULT and needs no outdoor work at all.
  SAFE ORDER 2. If the outdoor route runs, the learner works with their back to the sun and never looks toward it - not directly and not through a lens, filter, grating, CD, or camera.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Wear a hat and sunscreen, take drinking water, and work in the cooler part of the day, for no more than 30 minutes at a time.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Leave the dark water container OPEN in the sun; it is never capped or sealed.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Read the thermometer at fixed intervals from the shade, and come indoors at the scheduled end or at the first sign of overheating.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop instantly if anyone looks toward the sun through any optical device.
  STOP: Stop and move indoors at any sign of overheating.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Pour the water down the drain and dry the container, and return the CD or grating to its sleeve. Nothing hazardous is produced, and no image of the sun is captured by any means.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Skip all outdoor solar work: compute the sun's power output and lifetime from published solar-constant and mass data, and identify elements from published stellar spectra images. Paper and calculator only. This is the DEFAULT path.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Balloons pop and are a choking hazard for young children.
MITIGATION: Keep fragments away from young children; anyone with a latex allergy uses the elastic-band model.
HAZARD (emotional): Cosmological scale and deep time can be unsettling for some learners.
MITIGATION: Pace the content, keep the focus on evidence and reasoning, and allow the learner to pause at any point.
SUPERVISION: you may work on this independently. Tell an adult before you start anyway.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Ask about latex allergy before a balloon is opened; if anyone present has one, use the elastic-band model instead.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Mark the dots on the deflated balloon and measure their spacing before inflating.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Inflate in stages, measuring after each stage, keeping the balloon away from every face.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Deflate it deliberately rather than popping it.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Switch to the elastic-band model if anyone present has a latex allergy.
  STOP: Pause if the scale content becomes distressing.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Put whole balloons and every fragment straight into the bin - fragments are a choking hazard for young children. Recycle the paper. Nothing hazardous is produced.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Model expansion with dots drawn on an elastic band stretched along a ruler, then fit published redshift-distance data by hand. No balloon, paper and ruler only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Balloons pop and are a choking hazard for young children.
MITIGATION: Keep fragments away from young children; anyone with a latex allergy uses the elastic-band model.
HAZARD (emotional): Cosmological scale and deep time can be unsettling for some learners.
MITIGATION: Pace the content, keep the focus on evidence and reasoning, and allow the learner to pause at any point.
SUPERVISION: you may work on this independently. Tell an adult before you start anyway.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Ask about latex allergy before a balloon is opened; if anyone present has one, use the elastic-band model instead.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Mark the dots on the deflated balloon and measure their spacing before inflating.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Inflate in stages, measuring after each stage, keeping the balloon away from every face.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Deflate it deliberately rather than popping it.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Switch to the elastic-band model if anyone present has a latex allergy.
  STOP: Pause if the scale content becomes distressing.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Put whole balloons and every fragment straight into the bin - fragments are a choking hazard for young children. Recycle the paper. Nothing hazardous is produced.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Model expansion with dots drawn on an elastic band stretched along a ruler, then fit published redshift-distance data by hand. No balloon, paper and ruler only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Warm water used for the convection model can scald, and glass can crack from thermal shock.
MITIGATION: Keep water below 50 degrees Celsius, use a plastic or heatproof container, and let an adult pour.
HAZARD (physical): Food colouring stains surfaces and clothing.
MITIGATION: Work over a tray with old clothing or an apron.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Put on an apron and work over a tray; food colouring stains permanently.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Check the container for cracks before it is filled, and never pour warm water into cold glass.
  SAFE ORDER 3. An adult fills the container and confirms with the thermometer that the water reads below 50 degrees Celsius before it is placed.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Add colouring with a dropper from the side, without moving the container.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Let the water cool before the container is emptied or moved.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if the thermometer reads above 50 degrees Celsius. Water temperature is judged with the thermometer, never with a hand.
  STOP: Stop if a container shows any crack.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Pour the cooled coloured water down the drain with the tap running and rinse the container; wipe the tray and any stained surface immediately. A cracked container is wrapped in thick paper and tape before binning, never put in loose.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Do the convection strand from a published thermal-convection diagram sequence and complete the seafloor age mapping with coloured pencils on a printed map. No water, paper only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Warm water used for the convection model can scald, and glass can crack from thermal shock.
MITIGATION: Keep water below 50 degrees Celsius, use a plastic or heatproof container, and let an adult pour.
HAZARD (physical): Food colouring stains surfaces and clothing.
MITIGATION: Work over a tray with old clothing or an apron.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Put on an apron and work over a tray; food colouring stains permanently.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Check the container for cracks before it is filled, and never pour warm water into cold glass.
  SAFE ORDER 3. An adult fills the container and confirms with the thermometer that the water reads below 50 degrees Celsius before it is placed.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Add colouring with a dropper from the side, without moving the container.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Let the water cool before the container is emptied or moved.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if the thermometer reads above 50 degrees Celsius. Water temperature is judged with the thermometer, never with a hand.
  STOP: Stop if a container shows any crack.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.

  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Soil and outdoor materials carry bacteria and sharp fragments.
MITIGATION: Cover any cut or graze with a waterproof dressing before handling soil, wear gloves, keep hands away from the face, wash thoroughly afterwards, and never use soil from an area treated with pesticide or near a roadway.
HAZARD (physical): Soil on kitchen equipment contaminates everything used with it afterwards.
MITIGATION: The trays, cups, and measuring container are labelled for this investigation and never return to food use. Nothing from this investigation is washed in a kitchen sink.
HAZARD (physical): Water and soil together make surfaces slippery, and soil runoff blocks indoor drain traps.
MITIGATION: Work outdoors or over a large tray, clean spills immediately, and pour all runoff outdoors onto ground or through a strainer into an outdoor drain - never down a kitchen or bathroom sink.
HAZARD (privacy): Photographing or logging a field site can reveal where the family lives.
MITIGATION: Record substrate type, slope, and conditions only. No address, GPS coordinate, or identifiable landmark is recorded, and no photograph is required.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Use only the trays, cups, and measuring container labelled for this investigation. None of them has been used for food and none returns to food use.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Confirm the soil source with the adult: never soil from a treated area, a roadside, or an unknown source.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Cover any cut or graze with a waterproof dressing and put on gloves before touching soil, sand, or gravel.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Work outdoors or over a large tray, cleaning spills immediately so no surface becomes slippery.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Keep hands away from the face throughout and wash them thoroughly before coming indoors.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if soil source is unknown or possibly contaminated.
  STOP: Stop outdoor work near any road, steep bank, or water body.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Return the soil, sand, and gravel outdoors. Pour all muddy runoff outdoors onto ground, or through a strainer into an outdoor drain - NEVER down a kitchen or bathroom sink, where it blocks the trap. The trays, cups, measuring container, and gloves are washed outdoors, stay out of the kitchen, and never return to food use.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Compare infiltration through sand, gravel, and packed soil in three cups on a tray indoors, or work entirely from a published watershed dataset. Kitchen materials or paper.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Use only the trays, cups, and measuring container labelled for this investigation. None of them has been used for food and none returns to food use.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Confirm the soil source with the adult: never soil from a treated area, a roadside, or an unknown source.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Cover any cut or graze with a waterproof dressing and put on gloves before touching soil, sand, or gravel.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Work outdoors or over a large tray, cleaning spills immediately so no surface becomes slippery.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Keep hands away from the face throughout and wash them thoroughly before coming indoors.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if soil source is unknown or possibly contaminated.
  STOP: Stop outdoor work near any road, steep bank, or water body.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Return the soil, sand, and gravel outdoors. Pour all muddy runoff outdoors onto ground, or through a strainer into an outdoor drain - NEVER down a kitchen or bathroom sink, where it blocks the trap. The trays, cups, measuring container, and gloves are washed outdoors, stay out of the kitchen, and never return to food use.

ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.

lesson_flow.title: Safety review before any material is handled
lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (privacy): Mapping local hazards and resources can disclose where the family lives.
MITIGATION: Analyse a region at county scale or larger, or a region the family does not live in. Never record a home address or precise location.
HAZARD (emotional): Natural hazard content can be frightening, especially after a local event.
MITIGATION: Keep the framing on preparation, mitigation, and documented responses; the learner may choose a different region at any point.
SUPERVISION: you may work on this independently. Tell an adult before you start anyway.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Choose a region at county scale or larger, or one the family does not live in, before any map is opened.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Work from printed or adult-approved maps only; no address, coordinate, or identifiable landmark is recorded.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Build the argument and the evidence table on paper.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Change region at any point if the hazard content becomes distressing.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if the analysis begins to require the family's precise location.
  STOP: Switch regions if hazard content becomes distressing.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.

  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: File or recycle the printed maps and notes. No location data is stored, uploaded, or shared. Nothing hazardous is produced.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Use a supplied printed regional case study rather than searching sources, and complete the argument on paper. No online work required.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
